# Development Optimization Passes List

<!-- Don't bother formatting this. -->
<!-- mdformat global-off -->

This is an automatically generated list of all internal xls developtment
optimization passes available with the default `opt_main`. Normal optimization
passes may be found
[here](https://google.github.io/xls/passes_list/).
This is generated automatically based on comments in the header files.

!!! WARNING
    These passes are mostly intended for debugging and development use cases by
    the XLS development team and allow for the manipulation of ir files in ways
    that may not be desirable for general optimization use.

If the opt level is set below 'Min opt level' the pass will act as a no-op.

If the opt level is set above 'Cap opt level' the pass (or passes within the
compound pass) will be executed with the opt level capped to the specified
value.

!!! WARNING
    Many of these passes have descriptions generated by the Gemini LLM and may
    not accurately reflect the behavior of the passes. As time goes on manual
    verification or editing of the pass descriptions may be done to improve
    accuracy.


## assert_and_cover_removal - Assert and cover removal {#assert_and_cover_removal}


!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`AssertAndCoverRemovalPass` (`assert_and_cover_removal`) is a development
pass that strips all `assert` and `cover` operations from a `FunctionBase`.

During IR debugging, optimization investigation, or area/delay experiments,
verification operations (`assert` and `cover`) can keep condition cones and
token chains alive. Removing them allows developers to inspect or synthesize
the pure datapath and control logic in isolation.

### How It Works

The pass iterates over all nodes in the `FunctionBase`:
* **`Assert` nodes (`Op::kAssert`)**: Because an `assert` takes an input
  `token` as `operand(0)` and produces a `token`, the pass bypasses the
  assertion in the token graph by replacing all uses of the `assert` node
  with `n->operand(0)` and then removing the `assert` node.
* **`Cover` nodes (`Op::kCover`)**: Because a `cover` returns an empty tuple
  `()` and must have no users (`XLS_RET_CHECK(n->users().empty())`), the pass
  removes the `cover` node directly.

Any condition logic feeding only the removed `assert` or `cover` nodes
becomes dead and can be cleaned up by a subsequent `DeadCodeEliminationPass`.

### Example

```
// Before
fn checked_add(tkn: token, x: bits[8], y: bits[8]) -> (token, bits[8]) {
  sum: bits[8] = add(x, y)
  no_ovf: bits[1] = uge(sum, x)
  assert_tkn: token = assert(tkn, no_ovf, message="overflow", label="ovf")
  cover_max: () = cover( eq(sum, literal(value=255)), label="max_sum")
  ret result: (token, bits[8]) = tuple(assert_tkn, sum)
}
```

After `AssertAndCoverRemovalPass`:

```
// After
fn checked_add(tkn: token, x: bits[8], y: bits[8]) -> (token, bits[8]) {
  sum: bits[8] = add(x, y)
  no_ovf: bits[1] = uge(sum, x)
  ret result: (token, bits[8]) = tuple(tkn, sum)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/remove_assert_and_cover_pass.h)






## decompose_dataflow - Decompose dataflow {#decompose_dataflow}


Decompose and flatten all compound data type dataflow. This replaces all
array and tuple operations with operations on base values except directly
around externally visible values.

This pass is meant for testing and measurement.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`DecomposeDataflowPass` flattens compound dataflow (tuples and arrays) across
a `FunctionBase` into operations on scalar leaf values (`bits`, `token`, and
empty tuples `()`). Compound types are immediately decomposed into
`LeafTypeTree<Node*>` representations at their sources and are only
reconstituted at operations that require aggregate operands or at function
return boundaries.

### How It Works

The pass traverses nodes in topological order with `DecomposeDataflowVisitor`
(a subclass of `DataflowVisitor<Node*>` backed by a `StatelessQueryEngine`):

1. **Leaf Decomposition (`DefaultHandler`, Tuples, and Literals)**:
   * Tuple construction (`tuple`), tuple indexing (`tuple_index`), and array
     construction (`array`) are tracked directly in `LeafTypeTree<Node*>` by
     `DataflowVisitor` without requiring intermediate aggregate operations.
   * Compound source operations (`param`, `state_read`, `receive`, `literal`,
     `umulp`, and `smulp`) are decomposed into trees of leaf-typed nodes via
     `ToTreeOfNodes`.

2. **Compound Equality (`eq` and `ne`)**:
   * An `eq` comparing two compound operands is replaced by zipping their
     corresponding leaf pairs with leaf-level `eq` nodes and combining the
     results with an N-ary `and` (`NaryAndIfNeeded`).
   * A `ne` comparing two compound operands zips the leaf pairs with
     leaf-level `ne` nodes and combines them with an N-ary `or`
     (`NaryOrIfNeeded`).

3. **Selects and Gates (`sel`, `priority_sel`, `one_hot_sel`, `gate`)**:
   * `JoinElements` converts any select over compound cases into a tree of
     leaf-level selects (`CloneSelectLike` per leaf element).
     `HandleOneHotSel` explicitly routes through `Join` even when the
     selector is not proven one-hot so aggregate `one_hot_sel` nodes are
     always decomposed.
   * `HandleGate` decomposes a `gate` on a compound value into individual
     leaf-level `gate` operations sharing the scalar condition.

4. **Array Operations**:
   * **`array_index`**: Steps through each index operand (`IndexOneArray`).
     If `StatelessQueryEngine::IsAllZeros(idx)` holds, the constant index
     sub-tree is selected directly (clamped to the last element). Otherwise,
     the index is zero-extended if narrower than
     `MinBitCountUnsigned(array_size)` and a leaf-level `sel` is created for
     each leaf element across all array entries (using the last array entry
     as `default_value`).
   * **`array_update`**: For each element in the array tree, compares each
     index operand to the element's static index via `CompareLiteral`,
     combines the match bits with `NaryAndIfNeeded`, and emits a 2-way `sel`
     between the original leaf and the update leaf (skipping elements whose
     index exceeds the maximum value representable by the index bitwidth).
   * **`array_slice`**: Computes per-element indices `start + i` (clamping to
     `source_array_size - 1` when `i >= source_array_size` and zero-extending
     `start` if needed to avoid overflow) and indexes the array tree for each
     sliced element via `IndexOneArray`.
   * **`array_concat`**: Concatenates the leaf node vectors of all input
     array trees directly.

5. **Boundary Reconstitution (`HandleReconstituteOp` and Return Value)**:
   * Operations that cannot be decomposed (`invoke`, `map`, `counted_for`,
     `trace`, `send`, and `next`, except no-op `next` nodes where
     `IsNoOpNext` is true, which are left untouched) have their compound
     operands rebuilt via `FromTreeOfNodes` and their outputs re-decomposed
     via `ToTreeOfNodes`.
   * For a `Function`, the return value is rebuilt from its leaf tree via
     `FromTreeOfNodes`.

### Example

```
// Before
fn sel_tuple(p: bits[1], a: (bits[8], bits[16]), b: (bits[8], bits[16]))
    -> (bits[8], bits[16]) {
  ret chosen: (bits[8], bits[16]) = sel(p, cases=[a, b])
}
```

After `DecomposeDataflowPass` (followed by dead-code cleanup of the original
aggregate `sel`):

```
// After
fn sel_tuple(p: bits[1], a: (bits[8], bits[16]), b: (bits[8], bits[16]))
    -> (bits[8], bits[16]) {
  a_0: bits[8] = tuple_index(a, index=0)
  a_1: bits[16] = tuple_index(a, index=1)
  b_0: bits[8] = tuple_index(b, index=0)
  b_1: bits[16] = tuple_index(b, index=1)
  sel_0: bits[8] = sel(p, cases=[a_0, b_0])
  sel_1: bits[16] = sel(p, cases=[a_1, b_1])
  ret chosen: (bits[8], bits[16]) = tuple(sel_0, sel_1)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/decompose_dataflow_pass.h)






## literalize_zero_bits - Literalize zero bits {#literalize_zero_bits}


!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`LiteralizeZeroBits` (`literalize_zero_bits`) replaces all non-literal,
non-parameter operations that produce a zero-width bit vector (`bits[0]`)
with a constant `bits[0]` literal (`value=0`).

Because a `bits[0]` type carries zero bits of runtime information, any pure
computation producing `bits[0]` always evaluates to the unique zero-bit
value. Replacing such nodes with a `Literal` of `UBits(0, 0)` severs data
dependencies on their operands, simplifying the IR graph and allowing dead
code elimination to remove upstream logic that only feeds zero-width values.

### How It Works

The pass iterates over all nodes in the `FunctionBase` and checks whether
each node `n` satisfies:
* `n->GetType()->IsBits()` with `bit_count() == 0`,
* `!n->Is<Literal>()` (already a literal), and
* `!n->Is<Param>()` (parameters are preserved so the function signature and
  parameter list remain valid).

Every matching node has its uses replaced with a new `Literal` node holding
`Value(UBits(0, 0))`.

### Example

```
// Before
fn f(x: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  empty_slice: bits[0] = bit_slice(x, start=0, width=0)
  ret result: bits[8] = concat(empty_slice, x)
}
```

After `LiteralizeZeroBits`:

```
// After
fn f(x: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  lit_zero_bits: bits[0] = literal(value=0)
  ret result: bits[8] = concat(lit_zero_bits, x)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/literalize_zero_bits_pass.h)






## proc_state_legalization_shim - Proc State Legalization Pass {#proc_state_legalization_shim}


Compatibility shim to use the scheduling pass 'ProcStateLegalizationPass' in
the optimization pass pipeline for modernizing procs.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`ProcStateLegalizationPassShim` (`proc_state_legalization_shim`) is an
`OptimizationPass` wrapper around the scheduling pass
`ProcStateLegalizationPass`. Because `ProcStateLegalizationPass` inherits
from `SchedulingFunctionBasePass` and normally executes inside the scheduling
pipeline, this shim constructs a package-wide `SchedulingContext`
(`SchedulingContext::CreateForWholePackage`) and default
`SchedulingPassOptions` so proc state legalization can be invoked directly
from `opt_main` and optimization pass pipelines when modernizing or testing
procs.

### What the Wrapped `ProcStateLegalizationPass` Does

For each `Proc` in the package (non-proc `FunctionBase`s are skipped),
`ProcStateLegalizationPass` legalizes every `StateElement` in three steps:

1. **Mutual Exclusion Assertions (`AddMutualExclusionAsserts`)**:
   * **Write Mutual Exclusion (`AddNextValueMutualExclusionAssert`)**: If a
     state element has two or more `next_value` (`Next`) nodes, concatenates
     all of their predicates (`__<state>__next_value_predicates`), applies
     `one_hot(..., lsb_prio=true)` and slices off the MSB, compares equality
     with the concatenated predicates (`__<state>__at_most_one_next_value`),
     and emits an `assert` labeled
     `__<state>__at_most_one_next_value_assert` verifying that at most one
     `next_value` fires in any activation.
   * **Read Mutual Exclusion (`AddStateReadMutualExclusionAssert`)**: If a
     state element has two or more `state_read` nodes, similarly concatenates
     their predicates (substituting `literal(1)` for any unpredicated read)
     and emits an `assert` labeled `__<state>__at_most_one_read_assert`
     verifying that at most one `state_read` is active at a time.

2. **Write-Without-Read Assertions (`AddWriteWithoutReadAsserts`)**:
   If a state element has one or more `next_value` nodes and all of its
   `state_read` nodes are predicated, computes the disjunction of all read
   predicates (`__<state>__state_read_predicates_nary_or`). For each
   `next_value` node, emits an `assert` labeled
   `__<state>__next_<id>_without_read_assert` checking
   `any_read_active | !next_predicate`, ensuring a state update never fires
   when the state read is disabled.

3. **Default `next_value` Generation (`AddDefaultNextValues`)**:
   Ensures every state element has an explicit state update under all
   conditions:
   * If any `next_value` is unconditional, or if an existing no-op
     `next_value` (`IsNoOpNext`) already guards `nor(other_predicates)` (so
     the pass is idempotent), no default is added. (When run in the
     scheduling pipeline with `default_next_value_z3_rlimit` set, a solver
     can also prove the predicates exhaustive; the shim uses default
     `SchedulingPassOptions` where this limit is unset.)
   * If no `next_value` nodes exist for the state element, emits a default
     `next_value(param=state, value=state_read, predicate=read_pred)` for
     each `state_read`.
   * Otherwise, computes `__<state>__no_explicit_next_active =
     nor(predicates...)` and, for each `state_read`, adds a default
     `next_value` holding the state unchanged (`value=state_read`) when
     `no_explicit_next_active` (ANDed with `state_read->predicate()`, if
     present) is true.

### Example

```
// Before
proc counter(st: bits[32], init={0}) {
  en: bits[1] = ...
  inc: bits[32] = add(st, literal(value=1))
  next_inc: () = next_value(param=st, value=inc, predicate=en)
}
```

After `ProcStateLegalizationPassShim`, an explicit default `next_value` is
added to retain `st` when `en` is false:

```
// After
proc counter(st: bits[32], init={0}) {
  en: bits[1] = ...
  inc: bits[32] = add(st, literal(value=1))
  next_inc: () = next_value(param=st, value=inc, predicate=en)
  __st__no_explicit_next_active: bits[1] = not(en)
  st_default_st: () = next_value(
      param=st, value=st, predicate=__st__no_explicit_next_active)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/proc_state_legalization_pass_shim.h)






## remove_identifiers_unsafe - UNSAFE: Remove all identifiers {#remove_identifiers_unsafe}


A pass version of 'remove_identifers_main'. Running this pass will rewrite
the package to remove the names of all functions, procs, nodes, channels,
etc.

This should only be used while investigating optimizer behavior using the
ir-visualizer or other tools.

!!! WARNING
    This pass does not preserve externally visible names. Once run on a design
    the various io-constraint and other configs which rely on naming pieces of
    the design will not work. This pass is only for dev/ investigatory purposes.

!!! NOTE
    This pass **does not** preserve the id number of nodes.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`RemoveIdentifiersPass` (`remove_identifiers_unsafe`) anonymizes an XLS
`Package` in-place by stripping human-readable names and source location
information from functions, procs, blocks, channels, state elements,
registers, and IR nodes. It provides an optimization-pass interface to the
`StripPackage` utility (`remove_identifiers_main`).

### How It Works

1. **Constructing a Stripped Clone (`StripPackage`)**:
   The pass calls `StripPackage(p, options_)` (where default `StripOptions`
   set `new_package_name = "subrosa"` and enable `strip_location_info`,
   `strip_node_names`, `strip_function_names`, `strip_chan_names`, and
   `strip_reg_names`):
   * **Source Locations**: File-number mappings (`fileno_to_name`) are
     omitted and every node's `SourceInfo` is reset to an empty
     `SourceInfo()` when `strip_location_info` is true.
   * **Channels**: Package-scoped and proc-scoped channels are renamed
     sequentially to `chan_0`, `chan_1`, etc. when `strip_chan_names` is
     true.
   * **Functions, Procs, and Blocks**: Cloned in post-order
     (`FunctionsInPostOrder`) and renamed sequentially to `function_<N>`,
     `proc_<N>`, or `block_<N>` using a shared counter when
     `strip_function_names` is true.
   * **State Elements and Registers**: Within each proc, state elements are
     renamed to `state_0`, `state_1`, etc. when `strip_node_names` is true.
     Within each block, registers are renamed to `register_0`, `register_1`,
     etc. and the clock port is renamed to `"clock"` when `strip_reg_names`
     is true.
   * **Nodes**: When `strip_node_names` is true, `Param` nodes are renamed to
     `"param"` (auto-uniquified by XLS as `param`, `param__1`, etc.),
     `PortNode`s are renamed to `"port"`, and all other nodes have their
     explicit names cleared via `ClearName()` so they print using their
     opcode and newly assigned node ID (e.g., `add.3`).

2. **In-Place Package Replacement (`RunInternal`)**:
   The pass clears the original package `p` (clearing `Top`, removing all
   existing `FunctionBase`s and `Channel`s, and calling `ClearFiles()`),
   imports the anonymized contents from the temporary stripped package via
   `p->ImportFromPackage(new_p.get())`, restores the renamed `Top` entity via
   `p->SetTopByName(...)`, and rebuilds side tables on every `FunctionBase`.
   Its redundancy guard is `RedundancyGuard::Never()`.

### Example

```
// Before
fn compute_checksum(header: bits[16], payload: bits[16]) -> bits[16] {
  xor_val: bits[16] = xor(header, payload, id=10, pos=[(0,1,5)])
  ret inverted: bits[16] = not(xor_val, id=11, pos=[(0,2,5)])
}
```

After `RemoveIdentifiersPass`:

```
// After
fn function_0(param: bits[16], param__1: bits[16]) -> bits[16] {
  xor.3: bits[16] = xor(param, param__1, id=3)
  ret not.4: bits[16] = not(xor.3, id=4)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/remove_identifiers_pass.h)






## remove_one_hot_sel - One Hot Select Removal Pass {#remove_one_hot_sel}


Pass which replaces OneHotSelects with equivalent Selects without regard to
profitability concerns. This pass is meant for investigation and analysis use
only and should not be used for normal optimization pipelines.

To avoid extreme proliferation of nodes, we only translate OneHotSelects with
a selector bitwidth <= 16.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`RemoveOneHotSelectPass` (`remove_one_hot_sel`) is a debugging and analysis
pass (not included in default optimization pipelines, but invokable
explicitly via `opt_main`) that expands `one_hot_sel` operations into
exhaustive `sel` operations over all $2^N$ possible selector values,
regardless of profitability.

Because `one_hot_sel` ORs together the selected cases whenever multiple
selector bits are high (and produces zero when no selector bits are high),
converting an $N$-bit `one_hot_sel` without assuming one-hotness requires
enumerating all $2^N$ bit patterns of the selector.

### How It Works

The pass visits nodes in topological order (`context.TopoSort(f)`) and
processes each `OneHotSelect` node `ohs`:

1. **Width Guard (`kMaxBits = 16`)**:
   If the selector bitwidth exceeds `kMaxBits` (`16`), the node is skipped to
   prevent exponential blowup beyond $2^{16} = 65,536$ cases.

2. **Exhaustive `sel` Construction**:
   For a selector of width $N \le 16$, the pass replaces `ohs` with a
   `sel(selector, cases=new_cases)` having no `default_value` (since all
   $2^N$ selector values are covered), where `new_cases` has $2^N$ entries:
   * **Case `0` (`selector == 0`)**: Emits a `Literal` of
     `ZeroOfType(ohs->cases()[0]->GetType())`.
   * **Cases `1` through $2^N - 1$**: Treats the case index $i$ as an $N$-bit
     mask (`UBits(i, N)`), collects every `ohs->cases()[idx]` for which bit
     `idx` of $i$ is `1`, and combines the selected cases with an N-ary
     bitwise `or` via `NaryOrIfNeeded` (which returns the single case node
     directly when $i$ is a power of two, or creates an `or` node named
     `<ohs>_cases_<idx0>_<idx1>...` when multiple bits are set).

### Example

```
// Before
fn f(s: bits[2], c0: bits[8], c1: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  ret ohs: bits[8] = one_hot_sel(s, cases=[c0, c1])
}
```

After `RemoveOneHotSelectPass` and `DeadCodeEliminationPass`:

```
// After
fn f(s: bits[2], c0: bits[8], c1: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  zero: bits[8] = literal(value=0)
  ohs_cases_0_1: bits[8] = or(c0, c1)
  ret res: bits[8] = sel(s, cases=[zero, c0, c1, ohs_cases_0_1])
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/remove_one_hot_select_pass.h)






## to_zero_ext - DebugPass: To ZeroExt Pass {#to_zero_ext}


Converts any canonicalized zero-exts back from concat(zero, ...) to zero_ext
since it generally makes for easier to read/visualize graphs. This pass
is not meant to be used as an optimization pass at all.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`ToZeroExtPass` (`to_zero_ext`) is a debugging and visualization pass that
converts `concat` operations with leading zero operands back into explicit
`zero_ext` operations.

During standard XLS optimization pipelines, passes such as narrowing or bit
slicing often canonicalize or decompose a `zero_ext` into a `concat` of a
zero literal and the narrower value. While convenient for bit-level
transformations, these extra zero literals and `concat` nodes can clutter IR
graphs in visualizers and debugging dumps. `ToZeroExtPass` restores them to
single-operand `zero_ext` nodes.

### How It Works

1. **Query Engine Setup**:
   Acquires a shared `PartialInfoQueryEngine` for the `FunctionBase` and
   iterates over nodes in topological order (`context.TopoSort(f)`).

2. **Matching Zero-Extension-Like Concats (`ZeroExtLike::Make`)**:
   For each `Concat` node `n`, the pass checks `ZeroExtLike::Make(n, *qe)`.
   A `Concat` matches if:
   * Its total bit width is greater than zero, and
   * Every operand except the last (least-significant) operand is proven to
     be all zeros (`qe.IsAllZeros(op)`).

3. **Replacement**:
   Replaces the matching `Concat` node with a `zero_ext` (`ExtendOp` with
   `Op::kZeroExt`) that extends the last operand (`ext_like->to_extend()`) to
   the full bit width of the `Concat` (`n->BitCountOrDie()`).

### Example

```
// Before
fn extend_val(x: bits[8]) -> bits[16] {
  zeros: bits[8] = literal(value=0)
  ret ext: bits[16] = concat(zeros, x)
}
```

After `ToZeroExtPass`:

```
// After
fn extend_val(x: bits[8]) -> bits[16] {
  ret ext: bits[16] = zero_ext(x, new_bit_count=16)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/to_zero_ext_pass.h)
